title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has released its response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards. It outlines steps to strengthen transparency, accountability, and governance of AI use in the public sector.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is developing rules to manage how artificial intelligence can be used in exams and qualifications. The guidance aims to ensure fairness, transparency, and security while keeping students and educators safe.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and build AI systems, highlighting the legal and technical challenges involved. It assesses the impact on creators, users, and the AI industry, and offers policy recommendations to balance innovation with copyright protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has replied to a House of Lords report that warns there is no room for complacency in artificial intelligence, stressing the need for responsible development and use across the country. It outlines plans to strengthen regulation, boost investment in research and skills, and protect public safety and rights while encouraging innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the roles, responsibilities, and scope of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence should be governed in relation to public standards, including the committee’s objectives, membership, and decision‑making processes. It also provides frequently asked questions that clarify the committee’s focus areas and the expected outcomes of its review.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into AI governance, outlining its perspective on how artificial intelligence should be regulated. The submission emphasizes the need for balanced oversight, transparency, and stakeholder engagement to ensure responsible AI development.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: AI is reshaping the rules for medical products by adding strict safety, efficacy, and transparency standards that account for machine‑learning behavior. The policy applies the AI White Paper principles to guide regulators in overseeing AI‑driven medical devices while promoting responsible innovation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organization the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user among countries of its size. It focuses on leveraging AI to improve defense capabilities and maintain strategic advantage while ensuring ethical and responsible use.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to make use of AI’s opportunities. It also details steps to identify and manage potential risks associated with AI deployment.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright‑protected works are used in building AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines the current status, challenges, and recommendations for aligning AI development with copyright law.
